answer: Trust-graph routing curbs Sybil attacks by bounding agent trust along transitive paths from seed nodes. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of building authentic peer ties, since fake nodes remain trapped behind sparse cuts. Adversaries cannot echo trust across boundaries, exposing mass replication as an algorithmic fable. When an unvetted agent's transaction voyage exceeds path capacity, routing fails. However, this topology inherently penalizes honest newcomers lacking social connections.
